openings.claim: Current locators tied to reservation identity may reduce second searches while retaining surname shelves and some cart storage.
openings.discriminator: Separate search time from burst waiting; match cart arrival volume and book size. Accurate addresses remaining slow would favor load dominance.
openings.probe: Compare pickups with movement-triggered locator updates; record arrival, service start, retrieval, completion, accuracy, second searches and update work.
openings.uncertainty: Identity checking capability and sustained upkeep feasibility are unconfirmed; shelving superiority and target achievement remain unproven.

openings.claim: Freeze evening locations, retaining new arrivals on the cart and postponing moves until closing.
openings.discriminator: Unchanged verified locations should reduce second searches without surname correction; mismatch-specific gains favor correction. Congestion or unchanged delays defeats freezing.
openings.probe: Trial a cart-fitting batch; privately record opening locations, searches, correct handoffs and preparation time.
openings.uncertainty: Arrival volume, book size, cart accessibility, identity checks and whole-window capacity are unknown.

openings.claim: Number existing shelf sectors and privately index readers to sectors, separating household surnames from physical addresses.
openings.discriminator: Compare mismatch retrieval with surname correction; sector indexing should tolerate changed household associations without moving books. Staleness or lookup overhead defeats it.
openings.probe: Trial one shelf section using divider cards and paper; verify reader-book associations and time retrieval and upkeep.
openings.uncertainty: Full-volume indexing cost, legibility, shelf capacity and private association verification are unconfirmed.

decision: Compare bounded probes before choosing. Every probe requires the existing clerk alone for handoffs; names and contacts behind the desk; only two shelves and one cart, no added furniture; all daily preparation and preparation corrections within ten clerk-minutes, stopping at the cap. Verify correct recipients. Synthetic stipulations establish no effects: assess at least 95% within two minutes and zero wrong-reader handoffs; interview representativeness remains unknown.
